issues.display_title: Issue #912: fix(import): a Mappedin location's phone, website, socials, hours and logo are dropped on import
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-912-import-tenant-profile.mp4

Found in #900: after a Mappedin import, every Information record arrives with only a title, a description, categories, photos and hyperlinks. The phone, website, social links, opening hours and logo the export carries are thrown away — so the info card is empty where the venue's own Mappedin map shows a full profile.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Repro

  1. /start → name the project → confirm location → import a Mappedin export with tenant data (the Square One export from #900 is the reported one; samples/mall-demo-consumer.zip has one location with hours) → Continue to Editor.
  2. Link any tenant polygon to its Information (e.g. Walmart) and open Edit Information.
  3. Contact is empty, Hours reads Closed all week, Media has no logo — while the same tenant on the venue's Mappedin site shows a phone, website, Facebook/Instagram, 07:00–23:00 daily and a logo.

Measured on the reported export (369 locations):

Field in locations.json Locations carrying it Imported
phone 303 no
website {label, url} 317 no
social[] {name, url} (facebook 244, instagram 271, twitter 5) 280 no — hardcoded socialMedia: []
openingHours[] (schema.org OpeningHoursSpecification) 332 no
logo (top level) 364 no — the converter reads details.icon, which this export never sets
details.description, categories, images, links yes

The schema is confirmed against @mappedin/mvf 3.0.0-beta.11: logo, phone, social, website, openingHours and searchTags are all first-class location fields.

What actually happens

convertLocations in src/lib/mappedin/convert.ts maps details.{name,description,icon}, images, links and categories and nothing else. LocationEntry in src/lib/mappedin/types.ts does not even declare the other fields, so the parser hands them through untyped and the converter never looks.

The Information type already has phone, website, socialMedia, weeklyHours, logo and searchTags, and the info card, search panel and Edit Information modal already render every one of them. This is a converter gap only.

Scope

Extend LocationEntry with the MVF fields and map them in convertLocations — detected fields only, nothing fabricated:

  • logo: top-level logo, falling back to details.icon.
  • phone: trimmed; an empty string stays absent.
  • website: { name: label || url, url }, URL through withScheme like the hyperlinks.
  • social[]: { platform, url } when the lowercased name is one of the eight SocialPlatform values; anything else is dropped rather than guessed.
  • openingHours[] → weeklyHours: every listed day becomes { type: "open", open, close }; 00:00–23:59/24:00 becomes open24; a day listed twice keeps its longest range (Boston Pizza lists Saturday as both 00:00–02:00 and 11:00–23:59); PublicHolidays is skipped; a day the export does not list stays absent, which the type already reads as closed; a location with no entries gets no weeklyHours at all.
  • searchTags: copied when present.

Tests

src/lib/mappedin/__tests__/convert.test.ts:

  1. A location with phone, website, socials, hours and a top-level logo lands with all of them on the Information record.
  2. details.icon still becomes the logo when there is no top-level logo.
  3. An unknown social name is dropped, and an empty phone stays absent.
  4. Hours: a dayOfWeek array fans out to each day; a day listed twice keeps the longest range; 00:00–23:59 becomes open24; an empty list leaves weeklyHours undefined.

issues.display_title: Issue #913: feat(import): carry a Mappedin anchor tenant's colour and logo onto its polygon — needs a ruling
issues.main_description_html:
Found in #900: on the venue's own Mappedin map an anchor tenant (Walmart) is drawn as a dark polygon carrying its logo; after import it is a plain untyped polygon with no colour and no logo.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

What the export carries

The reported export is the kind-less flavour (cms/layers.json, #736). Its anchor tenants sit on a dedicated Anchor layer — 12 geometries, 9 tenants (Simons, Sport Chek, Urban Planet, Gap, H&M, Shoppers Drug Mart, Holt Renfrew, Goodlife Fitness, Walmart) — and default-style.json gives each geometry its fill: #222222 for the anchors, #f5f5f5 for two of them. The logo is on the location record (top level logo, 364 of 369 locations) and is imported by #912.

The converter's LAYER_AREA_TYPE maps Wall, Void and Floor only, so an Anchor polygon becomes an ordinary room; default-style.json is not read at all.

Why this is not a converter change — needs a ruling

Setting type: "closed" + color on the Anchor polygons in the converter does not survive the first load, measured with levelToModel on the reported export:

level 1: walls=0 areas=270 engineWalls=0 manualAreas=270 roomNames=0 | Walmart:MANUAL, Sport Chek:MANUAL, …
level 2: walls=0 areas=401 engineWalls=0 manualAreas=401 roomNames=0 | Simons:MANUAL, Walmart:MANUAL, Gap:MANUAL, …

This flavour draws its walls as polygon bands, so the level has no wall layer, no detected room, and every polygon becomes a manual Area. PRD §7 rules that an Area is never Closed: levelToModel (src/lib/floorplanEditor/bridge.ts) clears a stored closed on the way in, AreaLayer.color is documented as Closed-only and never written for another type, and the Area toolbar offers no type, colour or logo control — only Delete area and Convert to room.

So today the reporter's path is manual: select the Walmart Area → Convert to room → type Closed → colour and logo (the logo is already on the record once #912 lands).

Pick one:

  1. Allow Closed on an Area — colour + logo on a standalone polygon. A PRD §7 change; touches levelToModel, the Area toolbar and the map/2D paint.
  2. Convert Anchor polygons to rooms on import — synthesize the wall loop the way Convert to room does, then type them Closed with the default-style colour. Automatic, stays inside PRD §7, but turns 12 polygons into walls the user did not draw.
  3. Leave it manual and close this as working as designed once #912 puts the logo on the record.

Scope, once ruled (options 1 or 2)

  • parse.ts: read default-style.json into a per-floor geometryId → color map (every group is { geometryAnchors[], color, … } in both flavours).
  • convert.ts: Anchor → Closed, area.color from that map. The kinds flavour has no anchor concept and no …WithImage anchors in any sample, so nothing changes there.

Tests

Once ruled: a noKinds() fixture with one polygon on the Anchor layer and a default-style.json group naming it — the area comes out type: "closed" with the group's colour, and a round trip through levelToModel keeps it.

issues.display_title: Issue #917: fix(editor): Convert To Room refuses an Area beside a wall it reuses (#865 regression)
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-917-convert-beside-wall.mp4

Found in #898: on the Square One import (prod project b7fca45c…, Level 2) Convert to room on "Pearle Vision" and "Kids Foot Locker & Fly Zone" fails with Couldn't convert this area into a room — the area is unchanged, over and over, while other polygons on the same level convert fine.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

What happens

Every polygon that fails sits beside a wall that already exists — a tenant converted a moment earlier, or an anchor loop #913 now builds on import. Converting the 270 Areas of the reported export's level 1 one after another (the way a user does) fails 23 times; converting each on an empty plan fails 2 (a 1-unit sliver and the walkway). The engine's own status reads couldn't build a room from this area: the dry-run detectRooms finds no face around the ring.

Root cause — three, one toast

  1. #865 fold gap. A ring edge within WALL_REUSE_TOL (3 units) of an existing wall folds into it: the wall is extended, no new wall is built. That puts the edge on the wall's line, up to 3 units from where the ring drew it — but the edges either side were still built from the ring's own corners, so every fold left a gap of up to 3 units at both ends. detectRooms fuses nodes 1 unit apart. The ring leaks, the room never closes. The #865 tests only cover rings whose every edge folds, so no fresh edge ever met a moved one.
  2. reusableWall takes a wall that merely touches. Its tie-break compares a zero overlap against the EPS floor (|0 − EPS| ≤ EPS) and accepts it, so the neighbour's wall carrying on past this ring's corner, a degree or two off, is "reused": extended back along its line, up to 3 units off the ring ("Koryo Korean Barbeque").
  3. labelPoint on the walkway. The 17 × 17 sample grid over the bbox misses a ring 20 units wide winding across a bbox thousands wide, and the fallback is the centroid — outside such a ring. The dry run then finds no room containing it and refuses one the plan plainly holds; a label lands off the polygon too.

Fix

  • convertAreaToRoom (src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/commands.ts): the corners of a folded edge move onto the reused wall's line; a corner shared by two folds moves to where their lines meet (the node the two walls already share); fresh edges are built from those corners; a reused wall is extended to reach a corner that landed past its span.
  • reusableWall (src/lib/floorplanEditor/floorplan/geometry.ts): overlap <= EPS is not a reuse — touching is not overlapping, as the function's comment always said.
  • labelPoint: when every grid sample misses, a horizontal scan between two consecutive vertex heights returns the middle of the widest interior run — inside by construction, holes respected.

Not changed: a ring thinner than 1 unit is still refused (the width filter is right), and a ring that touches itself ("Room 53" / "Room 60", a spike vertex) still gets this area crosses itself.

Evidence (square-one-mall.zip, Areas converted in file order)

level before after
1 (270 Areas) 23 refused 1 (0.95-unit sliver)
2 (401 Areas) — 0

Tests

  • convert-area-to-room.test.ts: a fold on one side only closes; a corner between two folds lands where the walls meet; a wall that merely touches an edge's end is left alone.
  • geometry.test.ts: labelPoint answers inside the real Square One walkway ring, and keeps out of a hole on a thin frame.

issues.display_title: Issue #921: feat(import): show imported Information descriptions in the Mappedin review modal
issues.main_description_html:
video-921-information-description.mp4

Demo by Developer

Part 1 of #901 (PRD: Mappedin Import Information And Event Review).

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

What

The Imported Mappedin File modal lists every Information record the file carries, but only by title. The row component already renders an optional description (LocationInfoSection, since #266) — extractLocations just never fills it in, so the modal never shows one even though the exports ship them (square-one-mall.zip: 330 of 369 locations have a description; mall-demo-consumer.zip: 24 of 34).

Scope (PRD §2, R2–R5)

  • src/lib/mappedin-import/extractLocations.ts: map LocationEntry.details.description into ImportLocation.description. Trim title and description. Omit description when blank, missing or whitespace-only — never a placeholder. Keep the Untitled location title fallback.
  • No UI change: LocationInfoSection already shows description under the title when present and nothing otherwise.
  • Wizard step 2 and editor Add Floor share the same modal, so both surfaces pick it up.

Tests

src/lib/mappedin-import/__tests__/extractLocations.test.ts:

  • description maps from details.description, trimmed
  • blank / whitespace-only / missing descriptions are omitted (no description key)

Done when

  • Information rows show title + description when the export has one, title only otherwise.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green.

issues.display_title: Issue #922: feat(import): review-only Event section in the Mappedin import modal
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-922-event-review-section.mp4

Part 2 of #901 (PRD: Mappedin Import Information And Event Review).

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

What

Add a review-only Event section to the Imported Mappedin File modal, between Information and Floors, listing Event-like records found in the uploaded ZIP. Visible even at count 0. Nothing from it is saved: eventRecords (MapThru Event Highlights) are never created or modified by confirming an import.

Data reality

No Mappedin export we have carries events: 15 sample ZIPs (both the kinds/ and the cms/ flavour, including samples/square-one-mall.zip) contain no event/deal/promotion file or key, and the MVF v1/v2/v3 specs (incl. the CMS Extension) define none. The extractor is therefore built against a fixture, not a real file: it reads events.json and deals.json at the export root and under cms/ (an array of { id?, title?, name?, description? }), and every export we have today shows the empty state. Anything else (missing file, invalid JSON, non-array, non-object entries) is ignored — never an import failure.

Scope (PRD §1, §3–§8)

  • src/components/setup/import-mappedin/types.ts: ImportEvent { id; title; description? }; ImportResult.events: ImportEvent[] (always an array).
  • src/lib/mappedin/parse.ts + types.ts: read the event files above into MappedinExport.events; MappedinSource.events in detectSource.ts ([] for editor TXT/JSON exports).
  • src/lib/mappedin-import/extractEvents.ts: title = title, then name, then Untitled event; description only when non-blank; ids are positional (event-<index>), like loc-<index> for Information. No inference from locations, categories, floors or buildings.
  • src/lib/mappedin-import/runImport.ts: events on the returned ImportResult; floors/buildings/locations/object counts and the unreadable/empty failures unchanged.
  • src/components/setup/import-mappedin/EventListSection.tsx: same collapsible pattern as LocationInfoSection (shared body), header Event, count badge incl. 0, read-only rows title + optional description, empty state No events found in this file., no edit/delete/link controls.
  • ImportSummaryModal.tsx: section order Information → Event → Floors with the existing separators; header/footer/actions untouched.
  • Wizard Continue to Editor / Add More Floors and editor Add Floor keep writing exactly what they write today — no eventRecords writes.

Tests

  • extractEvents.test.ts: title over name, name fallback, Untitled event, blank description omitted, no supported records → [], invalid/non-array file ignored.
  • runImport.test.ts: ZIP with events.json → result.events; the fixture ZIP and an editor JSON export → events: [].
  • EventListSection.test.tsx: count badge, rows with title + description, empty state at 0.
  • ImportSummaryModal.order.test.tsx: Information before Event before Floors.
  • mergeIntoProject regression: staging an import into a store that already holds Event Highlights leaves eventRecords untouched, and the merge output carries no eventRecords.

Done when

  • Event section shows below Information and above Floors, count 0 + empty copy on today's exports, rows on a ZIP with events.json.
  • Confirming an import creates/modifies no eventRecords.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green.

issues.display_title: Issue #925: Share card og:image probe reaches the backend directly instead of the app's own origin
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-925-share-card-probe.mp4

Part 1 of #858 (Open Graph meta tags for social link sharing). Follow-up to #250.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

What

The /v/{key} share card shipped in #250 (PR #776) is dead in production: every published project renders og:image=https://map-thru.com/og.png even when its screenshot exists. Verified on 2026-09-03 with curl -A facebookexternalhit against all 10 published projects — four of them (hBzHWZHm, 5TUj8avG, 9zg5XR6J, HtRJfJxe) answer 200 image/jpeg on /api/live/{key}/image, yet their HTML still points at the (404) brand card. The same key on a local dev server gets the right og:image.

Cause: ogImageFor in src/app/v/[key]/layout.tsx probes the screenshot by fetching the app's own public origin (https://map-thru.com/api/live/{key}/image, host taken from headers()) from inside the Next process. That self-fetch fails on the production VM (Caddy in front of :3003; the public hostname is not reachable from the box the way it is from the internet), the catch swallows it, and the metadata falls back to /og.png. It only works in development because the host is localhost.

Scope

  • src/app/v/[key]/layout.tsx: probe the backend object directly — HEAD {GOTHRU_API_URL}/v1/live/{key}/file?name=og.jpg, the exact URL the /api/live/[key]/image proxy already reads (the Go endpoint answers HEAD with 200 image/jpeg). Drop the next/headers dependency and the origin reconstruction entirely.
  • Share that upstream URL between the layout and src/app/api/live/[key]/image/route.ts (one small server-only helper) so the two can never drift.
  • Emit og:image with width: 1200, height: 630 — both the uploaded screenshot (cropToOgCanvas) and the brand card are that size, and Facebook needs the dimensions to render the image on the first share instead of only after a re-scrape.
  • Keep the existing behaviour otherwise: unknown key → generic card without probing; probe 404 / throw → brand card fallback.

Out of scope: the project name in the title (#858 part 2, backend) and the brand card asset itself (#858 part 3).

Tests

src/app/v/[key]/__tests__/metadata.test.ts:

  • the probe is sent to {GOTHRU_API_URL}/v1/live/{key}/file?name=og.jpg, never to the app's own host and never to /api/files
  • og:image / twitter:image carry width and height
  • 404 and thrown probe still fall back to /og.png; unknown key never probes

Done when

  • Production /v/{key} for a project published from Preview emits its screenshot as og:image, with dimensions.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green.

issues.display_title: Issue #926: Interim public/og.png brand card (1200×630) for landing and share-card fallback
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-926-og-png-brand-card.mp4

Part 3 of #858 (Open Graph meta tags for social link sharing).

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

What

The landing page metadata (src/app/page.tsx) and the /v/{key} fallback (src/app/v/[key]/layout.tsx) both point og:image at /og.png, and that file has never existed — public/README-og.md has been the standing request for a 1200×630 asset since July. The brand kit (#224) delivered logo options only, no social card. So a share of map-thru.com, or of any project without a screenshot (published before #250 shipped, or published from the dashboard where no map is mounted), shows no image at all on Facebook. public/ is served in production (/file.svg is 200), so the file is all that is missing.

Scope

  • Commit an interim public/og.png, 1200×630: plain brand card — "MapThru" wordmark, the landing tagline, map-thru.com — on the landing palette. No new dependency; rendered once with the Playwright already in the repo.
  • Update public/README-og.md: the file now exists as a placeholder; the designed card from the UI Design board replaces it in place (same path, same size).
  • No metadata change: the path and dimensions are already what page.tsx and the live layout reference.

Tests

src/app/__tests__/ogImage.test.ts: public/og.png exists, is a PNG, and its IHDR reads 1200×630 — the size the metadata promises.

Done when

  • https://map-thru.com/og.png is 200 image/png, 1200×630, after the next release.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green.
